title: Tiered rate-limit decay, burst-bank, and transparent overage invoicing PRD
creator: Maya Rivera
description: Problem: Customers with bursty traffic patterns see wasted reserved capacity and opaque overage charges. Objective: introduce a decay-based tiered rate-limit system (per-caller and per-route) that converts unused steady-state capacity into a short-lived burst-bank, expose detailed per-route overage visibility in invoices, and ensure metering fidelity for per-model cost multipliers. Scope: PRD covers rate-limit policy design, UI/console surfaces, metering/telemetry contract, invoice examples, and acceptance criteria. Out of scope: billing system payments flow changes, enterprise contract negotiation UI (handled in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Rate-limit policy: Implement a three-tier policy per-caller: steady-state window (S), burst-bank (B), and decay function (D). S defines sustained tokens/sec, B is an accumulated buffer that can be consumed for spikes. D decays unused S credits into B according to configurable half-life (default 7 days).
Per-route enforcement: Console allows mapping route -> rate profile; runtime enforces at request ingress with clear headers indicating remaining S and B balances on each response for observability.

Metering fidelity: Every token consumed must be annotated in event stream with route, caller_id, model_id, token_type (prompt/completion), and model_cost_multiplier. Telemetry must be compatible with existing billing ingestion (ENG-42110).

Billing visibility: Weekly and invoice-line level breakdowns show steady usage, burst usage (consumed from B), and overage events, with example invoices for three customer archetypes (steady, bursty, sustained overage).

Backward compatibility: Default behavior for existing customers remains unchanged until entitlements are opted-in. Enabling new policy for a customer must be explicit and auditable via console and API.
Performance: Enforcement must add <=1ms median p99 <=5ms latency overhead to request path in the canary region under representative load (see perf-run 2025-02-20).
Telemetry completeness: No more than 0.1% of requests can be missing required billing tags in a 24h sampling window during rollout.
UI/UX: Console shows per-caller S and B balances in near real-time, a chart of decay history, and a what-if simulator estimating invoice impact if burst is fully consumed.
Docs & SDK: Public docs updated and client SDKs return 'x-rw-s-balance' header and a client helper to surface warnings when B falls below thresholds.
Security & privacy: No new PII added to telemetry; entitlements changes recorded in audit logs and require 'manage-pricing' RBAC role.
billing_acceptance_criteria: Meter-to-invoice mapping: Every billed line item must map back to at least one metering event with fields {caller_id, route, model_id, token_count, unit_price}.
Overage detection: Overage must be detected within 10 minutes of occurrence and tagged for potential auto-remediation triggers (e.g., soft-throttle or notification).
Invoice examples: Deliver three templated invoice line breakdowns with clear labels: 'steady usage', 'burst usage (consumed from burst-bank)', 'overage'. Templates included in attachments.
Disputeability: Invoice-level metadata must include raw event ranges and a hash link to the summarized meter batch used for billing to speed dispute resolution.
Pro-rata and credits: If a customer transitions plans mid-cycle and burst-bank was consumed, pro-rata credits must be calculated and appear as a separate credit line with audit justification.

Cost-multipliers: Models with special multipliers (e.g., +2.5x for large-context models) must be applied before aggregating to invoice lines, and the math must match the estimator in the console simulator within 0.5%.
Edge cases: Empty responses, retries, and partial tokens must be idempotently handled so billing is stable under retries.
decision_log: 2025-02-10: Chose decay-based accumulation over per-calendar-window top-ups because it smooths incentives for sustained efficiency (decision by PM/Eng/Finance).
2025-02-12: Agreed on default half-life=7 days with admin-configurable range (1-30 days) to balance predictability and burst capacity (trade-off: UX simplicity vs flexibility).
2025-02-18: Opted to expose S/B balances via response headers rather than expanding API surface for fastest iteration and SDK support.
outstanding_questions: Should enterprise customers be able to opt-out of decay conversion and instead receive invoice credits? (Raised by Sales on 2025-02-19)
What is the expected storage cost for retaining per-request billing tags for 90 days vs 365 days? (Finance/Infra dependency)
Do we allow negative burst-banks (borrowed capacity) with an auto-payback window? Security and accounting implications pending.
implementation_notes: ENG-42110 will provide the metering schema extension for model_cost_multiplier and route tagging; implementation must be feature-flagged.
Runtime changes: Traffic router must maintain per-caller S and B counters in in-memory store with periodic persistence to shards for auditability.
Batching: Ensure prefix/KV cache interactions do not incorrectly attribute token consumption to B when previously cached prefixes are served. Add test coverage.
qa_plan: Unit tests for decay calculation, boundary conditions, and half-life overrides.
Integration test that simulates three-week usage pattern to validate decay behavior and B accumulation.
Canary rollout to 5% of tenants with synthetic traffic and daily metering audits for at least 72h before ramp.
Billing reconciliation runs comparing canary metering batches to invoice simulator output with tolerance <=0.5%.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal dogfood on staging (2 weeks) to validate telemetry and console surfaces.
Phase 1: Canary to self-serve customers with opt-in toggle (5% of tenants) for 2 weeks.
Phase 2: Open to all new tenants by default, existing tenants opt-in via console for one billing cycle trial.
Phase 3: Post-launch 30-day review to consider making the policy default based on adoption and dispute rates.
notes: 2025-02-16: Kickoff with ENG, FINANCE, SALES — high-level alignment achieved; Sales asks for enterprise opt-out (recorded in outstanding_questions).
